headline: Bangladesh and Malaysia sign MoU to advance cultural cooperation
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's first foreign trip focuses on strengthening ties, labour market access, and counter-terrorism cooperation.
details: Bangladesh and Malaysia have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to advance cooperation in the field of culture. The two nations also exchanged bilateral notes on investment and research and capacity building in counter-terrorism.

Bangladeshi Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim held a one-on-one meeting in Putrajaya on Monday, followed by a bilateral meeting with their respective delegations.

The two leaders discussed advancing cooperation in trade, employment, and energy security. Prime Minister Tarique Rahman urged Malaysia to reopen its labour market and recruit more Bangladeshi workers.
The visit marks the first foreign trip for Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, with expatriate workers' welfare and employment opportunities being a primary focus of the visit.
Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman and Malaysian Foreign Minister Utama Haji Mohamad bin Haji Hasan signed the exchange of notes on behalf of their respective countries.

The visit marks the first foreign trip for Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, with expatriate workers' welfare and employment opportunities being a primary focus of the visit.

Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman and Malaysian Foreign Minister Utama Haji Mohamad bin Haji Hasan signed the exchange of notes on behalf of their respective countries.

headline_marked: Crimes against humanity: [[Verdict in Inu's case on June 30]]
headline: Crimes against humanity: Verdict in Inu's case on June 30
summary: International Crimes Tribunal-2 will deliver its decision on Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal (JaSaD) President Hasanul Haq Inu.
details: A three-member bench of the International Crimes Tribunal-2, led by Justice Nozrul Islam Chowdhury, has set June 30 for the verdict in a crimes against humanity case against Hasanul Haq Inu.
Inu, the President of Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal (JaSaD) and a former minister, faces eight charges including involvement in the murder of seven people in Kushtia during the 2024 July Uprising.
The former minister was arrested by police from Dhaka’s Uttara area on August 26, 2024.
Since his arrest, Inu has been questioned in police custody several times in connection with various cases.
caption:
Former minister Hasanul Haq Inu faces a verdict on crimes against humanity charges on June 30.

A three-member bench of the International Crimes Tribunal-2, led by Justice Nozrul Islam Chowdhury, has set June 30 for the verdict in a crimes against humanity case against Hasanul Haq Inu.

Inu, the President of Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal (JaSaD) and a former minister, faces eight charges including involvement in the murder of seven people in Kushtia during the 2024 July Uprising.

The former minister was arrested by police from Dhaka’s Uttara area on August 26, 2024.

Since his arrest, Inu has been questioned in police custody several times in connection with various cases.
